query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A single intervention of low-temperature aging (300–400°C for 1–4 hours) applied to an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy (e.g., Al0.5CoCrFeNiMg0.5, density ~5.2 g/cm³) with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic microstructure will suppress the growth of brittle stable intermetallic phases (e.g., B2-NiAl, Mg2Ni) while promoting the formation of a nanostructured, coherent precipitate distribution that enhances room-temperature compressive strength and ductility. This intervention will simultaneously improve corrosion resistance by stabilizing a Cr-rich passive oxide layer and enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance by forming a protective Al2O3/Cr2O3 duplex scale, without compromising the low-density requirement.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy (e.g., Al0.5CoCrFeNiMg0.5) with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, density <6 g/cm³, exhibiting brittle intermetallic networks that limit ductility and corrosion resistance.
generation.intervention: Low-temperature aging at 300–400°C for 1–4 hours in an inert atmosphere (e.g., argon) to induce controlled precipitation and phase stabilization without coarsening.

conditions.test_environment: Room-temperature compression, 3.5 wt% NaCl solution (corrosion), 800°C air (oxidation)

generation.structural_mediator: Nanostructured, coherent precipitates (e.g., L12-Al3Ni, B2-NiAl) within a disordered FCC/BCC matrix, suppressing brittle intermetallic network formation and promoting a homogeneous microstructure.
generation.mechanism: Aging at 300–400°C provides sufficient thermal energy for solute diffusion to form coherent, nano-sized precipitates that strengthen the matrix via Orowan bypassing and solid-solution hardening, while simultaneously stabilizing a Cr/Al-rich passive oxide layer that inhibits intermetallic growth and enhances corrosion/oxidation resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-processed baseline: (1) Room-temperature compressive yield strength increases by 20–30% with ductility retained or improved (>10% strain); (2) Corrosion current density decreases by 50–70% in 3.5 wt% NaCl; (3) Oxidation mass gain at 800°C for 100 hours decreases by 40–60% due to a protective duplex oxide scale.
generation.baseline: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight HEA with metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, exhibiting low ductility (<5% strain), high corrosion current density, and significant oxidation mass gain at 800°C.
generation.boundary: Composition: Al0.5CoCrFeNiMg0.5 (density ~5.2 g/cm³); Temperature: 300–400°C (aging); Exposure time: 1–4 hours; Test environments: Room-temperature compression, 3.5 wt% NaCl (corrosion), 800°C air (oxidation).
generation.uncertainty: The exact aging parameters (temperature/time) may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and initial microstructure. The formation of coherent precipitates may be limited if the alloy contains elements that promote rapid intermetallic growth at aging temperatures. The protective oxide scale formation may be compromised if the alloy contains elements that form volatile oxides (e.g., MgO).
generation.falsification_experiment: Perform low-temperature aging (300–400°C, 1–4 hours) on the as-processed Mg-containing lightweight HEA and compare its room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance (in 3.5 wt% NaCl), and high-temperature oxidation resistance (at 800°C for 100 hours) against an unaged control. If the aged sample shows no improvement in ductility, corrosion resistance, or oxidation resistance, or if the intermetallic network coarsens instead of being suppressed, the hypothesis is falsified.
